For every finite Juggler word w realized at n, J^{|w|}(n)^{2^{|w|}} ≤ n^{3^{#O(w)}}. If n ≥ 2 and 3^{#O(w)} < 2^{|w|}, then J^{|w|}(n) < n.

If n ≥ 2, A > 0, x^A ≤ n^B, and B < k·A, then x < n^k. EnvelopeState n x packages the free inequality x^A ≤ n^B, with even (A,B)→(2A,B) and odd (A,B)→(2A,3B). PowerBound is the special case A=2^|w|, B=3^{oddCount w}. A realized itinerary with 3^{oddCount w} < k·2^{|w|} therefore has T_w(n) < n^k. power_bound_contracts is the k=1 case. Escape square and cube cells are k=2 and k=3 instances. The leftover itinerary OOEOOEOOEOEOO has the cube gap 3^9 < 3·2^13 and not the square gap 3^9 < 2·2^13. This is not a halt theorem and not a cycle-exclusion theorem.

Hercher's Lemma 8 survives the exponential conjugacy, on the exponent, and the laboratory had already proved it under another name. Conjugating the Collatz odd step by u = x + 1 turns (3x+1)/2 into exactly u -> 3u/2; the Juggler's exact odd step on n = a^e turns, on the exponent, into exactly e -> 3e/2. Same map, same prime, same reason -- 3 is a 2-adic unit, so one step costs exactly one unit of v_2 and nothing else -- and the exact even step e -> e/2 costs the same unit, so the valuation drops by one per step whatever the letter and an exact run is monochrome, the letter being the parity of the base. COLLATZ CARRIES THE 2-ADIC INTEGER IN THE VALUE, THE JUGGLER IN THE EXPONENT. Hence one law at the two ends of x = 2^y: run(x) = v_2(x+1) (Hercher 2023, Lemma 8: k consecutive odd steps force x = -1 mod 2^k) and exactRun(n) = v_2(e(n)), where e(n) = max{e : n = a^e} and exactRun counts consecutive states at which the floor is not charged, that is consecutive squares. The Juggler half is kernel-checked as HasPowTwoDepth with hasPowTwoDepth_even_exact, hasPowTwoDepth_odd_exact and power_bound_eq_implies_pow_two_depth (j-saturation-budget, filed as a local arithmetic question in August); the converse half is isSquare_pow_three_iff. Exhaustive agreement to N = 10^6: 999 square states, 19859 non-square states, 100000 odd Collatz starts, no failure. THE FLOOR IS THE EXPONENTIAL OF THE FLOOR. Both pointwise bounds follow by the same product-formula step -- a nonzero integer with v_2 >= k has absolute value at least 2^k -- and both are attained: run(x) >= k forces x >= 2^k - 1, attained at 2^k - 1; exactRun(n) >= k forces n >= 2^(2^k), and on odd starts n >= 3^(2^k), attained at 3^(2^k) with word O^k. log(3^(2^k)) = 2^k log 3, so J-juggler-is-collatz-one-exponential-up holds pointwise and not only on the walk. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, WHICH IS THE POINT. Hercher's hypothesis is k consecutive odd LETTERS, a condition on the word that any cycle with a long run supplies free; the mirror's hypothesis is k consecutive EXACT steps, a condition on the integer that no word implies. The exponential moves the hypothesis from the word to the arithmetic, so the mirror is inert for cycles and for termination: no floor is raised, no m-cycle is excluded, and no Collatz bound is improved. Lemma 8 is quoted from hercher-2023-collatz-m-cycles, not reproved. A residual-shaped word O^a E^b is formally expanding iff 2^{a+b}<3^a. For a≥1 this is equivalent to a+b ≤ log₂(3^a), or b ≤ maxExpandingEvens(a). In particular a=2 or 3 forces b≤1, and a=4 forces b≤2. This is the syntactic expanding language, not a realized-orbit theorem.

For n≥2, PersistentOddResidual x y if and only if PersistentExpandingResidual x y. A contracting residual cannot overshoot, and 2^k=3^o is impossible for a nonempty residual. The expanding qualifier of a persistent residual is therefore redundant.

The expanding residual word grammar, or a finite residue-mod-8 successor automaton, is an independent obstruction to an infinite persistent expanding chain. Counterexamples: on n≥2 persistence already is expansion, so the attack reduces to T_w(n)>n; the OOE type self-loop 365→763→1749 exits odd-to-even at 4447; every odd class modulo 8 both continues and leaves the PE frontier. A finite run bound M is not proved and is not supplied by this grammar.

The integer exponent surplus of a finite Juggler word is E(w)=3^{#O(w)}-2^{|w|}, and E(w)>0 if and only if the itinerary is formally expanding. An expanding residual block O^a E^b with b≥1 has b<a. On an expanding itinerary, n^{3^{#O}}=n^{2^{|w|}+E(w)}. Relative slack multiplies under concatenation, and the slack numerator of a three-block word is n^{3^{o(v)+o(w)}}. The chain 365 --OOE--> 763 --OOE--> 1749 --OOE--> 4447 is a PersistentExpansionChain. This does not bound consecutive expanding persistent runs.

Read against a smooth profile, M_v - m_v of order f/v on a block of size f v, the first term is O(f) per value against a window mass of f v: the collapsed mass entering through the even branch is fair up to a relative O(1/v). Fate classes of the Juggler map are backward-closed (J n ∈ A ⟹ n ∈ A): the starts that reach 1 (reachesOne_backwardClosed), the starts that do not (not_reachesOne_backwardClosed), the basin Ancestor · m of any state m (ancestor_backwardClosed), and the divergent starts (escapes_backwardClosed); R and the divergent set are also forward-closed (reachesOne_floorPower, escapes_floorPower). Every start n ≥ 1 reaches 1, or is an ancestor of a state m ≥ 2 on a cycle (Periodic m), or escapes (fate_trichotomy, from cycles_or_escapes), and the fates exclude one another: a start that reaches 1 or enters a cycle has a bounded orbit (reachesOne_bounded, cycle_basin_bounded, reachesOne_not_escapes, cycle_basin_not_escapes), and a start that reaches 1 is not an ancestor of a cycle state m ≥ 2 (reachesOne_not_cycle_basin). Lemma 1.1 of the fate-contagion note. Not a halt theorem.

The two exact productions of a backward-closed set A. Even block: if m ∈ A then every even n with m·m ≤ n < (m+1)(m+1) has J n = m (floorPower_even_block) and lies in A (even_block_mem); the block has at least m even elements (even_block_card). Odd generation of two-way closed fate classes (fate-contagion note, Theorem 6.1). Paper C Lemma 5.1 (recursion lemma). Let e_i ∈ [e_min, e_max] with 0 < e_min and e_max < 1, c_i real, λ > 0 with ζ := Σ_i c_i e_i^λ - 1 > 0, t_1 > 0, c_0 > 0. Let g : ℝ → ℝ satisfy g(t) ≥ Σ_i (c_i - η_i(t)) g(e_i t) - η_0(t) for all t ≥ t_1, where 0 ≤ η_i(t) ≤ c_i, Σ_i η_i(t) e_i^λ ≤ ζ/3 and η_0(t) ≤ (2ζ/3) c_0 for t ≥ t_1, and g ≥ c_0 on [e_min t_1, t_1]. Then g(t) ≥ c_0 t_1^{-λ} t^λ for all t ≥ e_min t_1 (recursion_lemma). The proof is the paper's induction on N over [e_min t_1, t_1 e_max^{-N}], with exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one supplying N. Weaker hypotheses than the paper's: e_min, e_max are bounds rather than the extrema, λ < 1 and g ≥ 0 are not needed. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. This is the abstract analytic step of Theorem 5.3; the three-source inequality (5.2) and its constants stay human proofs. The seed (Lemma 5.2) is Lean, row J-fate-seed. Conditional scale-averaged pressure theorem at the unconditional contagion threshold. Fix integers N0>=2 and k0>=0 with N0<2^(k0+1), and assume every integer from 1 through N0 reaches 1. Let C>1, theta>0, 0<q<1, eta>=0, a=1-q+q*exp(theta), pC=(1-1/C)/log_2(3), and r=C*(theta*pC-log(a))/log(2). For y=2^k set d=ceil(C*log_2(log(2*y)/log(N0))). Let Z_k be the sum of exp(theta*o_d(n)) over odd integer starts y<n<=2*y whose Juggler iterates at every time 0 through d exceed N0; o_d(n) counts odd states at times 0 through d-1. Set rho_k=Z_k/((2^k/2)*a^d). Suppose that for every epsilon>0 there exists a real D>=0 such that, for every integer K>=0, sum(rho_(k0+j),0<=j<K)<=D*K^(1+eta+epsilon). If r-eta>103/203, every positive integer reaches 1. ScaleAverage.pressure_average_conjecture proves precisely this conditional implication. Its Bound definition spells out the cumulative hypothesis, and liveOdds, oddPressure and rho define the actual stopped Juggler moments. Paper C Lemma 5.2 (seed). Every nonempty backward-closed A with a positive member contains some m ≥ 3 (exists_ge_three_of_backwardClosed: 1 maps to 2 maps to 4 through even blocks). For any such m and every y ≥ (m+1)^4, the log-mass of A on (√y, y] is at least c_A = (1 − 2/m^4)(3/8 · 1/(m+1) − 1/((m+1)^2 − 1)) (seed_lemma), and c_A > 0 (seed_constant_pos). Proof as in the paper: the even-block tree S_k of m lies in A and in [m^{2^k}, (m+1)^{2^k}); its log-mass grows by at least 1 − 2 m^{-2^k} per level; the product is at least 3/4 by the geometric series 1/(m^2 − 1) ≤ 1/8; at scale k = log2 log_{m+1} y the tree splits at floor(√y) into members above √y, members whose even blocks lie there, and at most one member equal to floor(√y). The integer form y = floor(x) is the paper's g_A(log x). Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. This is one hypothesis of Theorem 5.3; the production inequalities stay human proofs. Not a density theorem, not a halt theorem.

Paper C Lemma 4.1' (monotone pairing), with a corrected proof and the same constant. Hypotheses of Lemma 4.1 (steps in [a, b], 0 < a ≤ b ≤ 1/2, b ≤ 21a/20, (H−1) a ≥ 12) plus monotone steps: each half-cell colour receives at least H/3 − 2 terms, in both cell conventions. The proof printed until 2026-09-08 claimed every pair of consecutive cells (ρ, ρ') has min ≥ (ρ+ρ')/3, deduced from a step scale that 'drops by at most X/21 spread over the cells'; monotonicity does not give gradual change, and a = 10/41, b = 21/82 with points −2a, −a, 0, a, 2a, 2a+b, 2a+2b, … (nondecreasing steps) has the interior pair (3, 1), ratio 1/4. Corrected proof: (a) for interior i < j, ρ_j ≤ ρ_i + 1, because the ρ_i + 1 steps across cell i span more than 1/2 so one exceeds 1/(2(ρ_i+1)), every step inside cell j is at least that, and the ρ_j − 1 steps inside cell j span less than 1/2; (b) pair the interior cells consecutively, leave at most three cells (≤ 3G points) unpaired, so the scarcer colour has at least (H − 3G)/3 + S with S the surplus Σ (min − sum/3) over pairs, and it suffices that S ≥ G − 2; (c) G ≥ 7: 7g ≥ 5G so every pair has ratio ≥ 5/12 and S ≥ (H − 3G)/12 ≥ (21G − 23)/12 ≥ G − 2 using H ≥ 24G − 23; (d) 3 ≤ G ≤ 6, g ≥ 2: ratio ≥ 3/8 except (G, g) = (4, 2), where (a) gives {3,4}-pairs (≥ 3/7) before {2,3}-pairs (≥ 2/5) with at most one straddle, S ≥ (H − 18)/15 > 2; (e) G = 2: S ≥ 0; (f) G = 3, g = 1 (b > 1/4, 3b < 1, 7b < 2): after the first interior 1-cell all cells hold ≤ 2, adjacent (1,1) is impossible (three steps would span > 1), two consecutive pairs with six points are impossible (seven steps would span > 2), so any two consecutive {1,2}-pairs hold ≥ 7 points with ≥ 3 for the scarcer colour, S ≥ (H − 13)/15 − 1 ≥ 1. Adversarial search over 4.2 · 10^6 two-valued monotone profiles at 64 phases each (X ∈ [1, 6), b/a ∈ {1, 1.02, 1.04, 1.05}, all switch points and 64 phases): no violation, least slack 1.33 over H/3 − 2; fact (a) holds on every profile. Theorem A of the Tao-reduction note. If for some e > 1 − λ** = 0.5074… and all sufficiently large y, #{n odd in (y, 2y] : n does not reach 1} ≤ y (log y)^{−e}, then every positive integer reaches 1. Proof: every failure lies in the E-tree of an odd failure (forward closure), each E-tree level has log-mass ≤ 2/n₀ and at most 1 + log₂ log x levels meet [1, x], so the log-count of the failure set is ≪ (log x)^{1−e} log log x, contradicting fate contagion (J-fate-log-density) for any λ ∈ (1 − e, λ**). The E-tree bound, the dyadic sum and the contradiction given a contagion lower bound K (log x)^λ are Lean (tao_rate_implies_conjecture in FateTaoReduction.lean); the contagion bound itself (Theorem 5.3) stays a human proof, so this row is not Lean-verified. The same holds for the hypothesis stated over all n in (y, 2y], and in logarithmic form it is Corollary 4.5 of the fate note. A Tao-type almost-all theorem with the bounded target [1, N₀] and rate (log y)^{−0.53} would therefore prove the Juggler conjecture; for the Collatz map the analogous implication fails (thin preimage trees). Not a halt theorem: the hypothesis is not proved. The contagion hypothesis is discharged unconditionally at e > 103/203 = 0.50739 by Production.conjecture_of_tao_rate_averaged (J-oe-averaged-two-productions-reach-the-depth-two-ceiling), which is below Paper C's conditional 0.51. MEASURED (tao_reduction.unconditional_depth_drop): that moves the least unconditional cylinder depth from C = 23 to C = 19, and the pressure-form thresholds from 23, 50, 273, 1953 to 19, 41, 214, 1496 at q = 0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.62. Against lambda** itself nothing numerical moves -- those are the same 19, 41, 214, 1496 -- so what this buys is status, not constants.

Paper C Lemma 4.3 (bad fibers are thin), badness being ¬Good of row J-fate-fiber-parity. (i) bad_count_le: for u ≥ 10^6, #{m ∈ (u, 2u] : ¬Good m} ≤ 63 u^{2/3}. (ii) bad_logMass_le: for U ≥ 10^6 and every N, Σ_{m ∈ (U, N], ¬Good m} 1/m ≤ 306 U^{−1/3} (the paper's infinite sum, as a bound on every partial sum). Proof of (i): the increments of A_m = (3/2) m^{2/3} lie in [(m+1)^{−1/3}, m^{−1/3}] by Bernoulli both ways (Am_step_ge, Am_step_le); a bad m > u has {A_m + 22 u^{−1/3}} < 44 u^{−1/3} or {A_m} ∈ [1/2 − 2u^{−1/3}, 1/2 + 2u^{−1/3}) (bad_mem_arc; the shift makes the wrap-around arc a single arc); arc_count_le: a sequence increasing by at least d per step on (u, v] has at most (⌊φ(v)⌋ − ⌊φ(u+1)⌋ + 1)(w/d + 1) indices with fractional part in an arc [c, c+w) ⊆ [0, 1), by the fibre-per-integer-window count; with d = (2u)^{−1/3} (sharper than the paper's (3u)^{−1/3}), w/d = 44·2^{1/3} and 4·2^{1/3}, the windows number at most A_{2u} − A_u + 2 ≤ 0.882 u^{2/3} + 2 (2^{2/3} ≤ 1.588), and (0.882 u^{2/3} + 2)(48·2^{1/3} + 2) ≤ 63 u^{2/3} for u^{2/3} ≥ 10^4 (2^{1/3} ≤ 1.26). Proof of (ii): on one block (u, 2u] the bad log-mass is at most 63 u^{2/3}/u = 63 u^{−1/3} (bad_block_logMass_le); (U, N] ⊆ (U, 2^N U] which is the disjoint union of the blocks (2^i U, 2^{i+1} U], i < N (bad_sum_dyadic_le); (2^i U)^{−1/3} = (2^{−1/3})^i U^{−1/3} (eps_pow_two_mul); the geometric series gives 63 U^{−1/3}/(1 − 2^{−1/3}) and 2^{−1/3} ≤ 0.794 (0.794^3 ≥ 1/2) gives 63/(1 − 2^{−1/3}) ≤ 306. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3 together are the fiber input of the three-source inequality (5.2); Proposition 4.4 stays a human proof. Let x1 = T_{O^{a0} E}(n) and B = T_OE. If O^{a0} E follows at n, (OE)^r follows at x1, and B^r(x1) ≥ n, then 2^{2r+a0+1} ≤ 3^{a0+r}. Write R(a0) for the largest such r. Then R(2)=0, R(3)=1, R(4)=3. This is an AboveAnchor / isolated-prefix theorem, not a cycle-return theorem. On a CycleMin-shaped prefix this bounds isolated-OE transport before the first internal OO: r ≤ R(a0). In particular an a0=2 CycleMin cannot complete one OE after the first even while staying ≥ n, so its first internal OO, if it exists, is immediate (r=0). The same r=0 bound holds for a MinimalNonTerm realization of O^{2}E(OE)^r. Lean: isolatedOddSurvival_bound, isolated_oe_ge_implies_exponent, isolated_oe_lt_of_scale_gap, isolated_oe_r_max_two in FirstInternalOO.lean; aboveAnchor_isolated_two in MinimumRelative.lean; no_cycleMin_prefix_ooe_oe, cycleMin_isolated_two in CycleObstructions.lean; minimal_isolated_two in Minimal.lean. The suffix after that OO is not classified. This is not a Z5 family, not a length-11 census, and not a halt theorem.

Gap transfer (Paper A Theorem 4.10). On a Juggler CycleMin start n ≥ 2 with word w of length L and oddCount o, n · log n · min(o log 3 − L log 2, 1) ≤ 2 L (cycleMin_gap_transfer). Proof: Theorem 4.4 reads P(A − B) ≤ L A with A = 3^o, B = 2^L, P = n log n; if A ≤ B the left side is nonpositive, if A ≥ 2B then P ≤ 2L, and if B < A < 2B then Λ = log(A/B) ≤ (A − B)/B and P(A − B)/B ≤ LA/B ≤ 2L. Abstract form cycleMin_length_of_gap: any ε ≤ min(Λ, 1) gives n log n · ε ≤ 2L. The printed Corollary 4.11 display under the hypothesis L^{−13.3} ≤ Λ is cycleMin_length_of_rhin. Floor-free; the classical transcendence input is a hypothesis, not a Lean theorem. Not a halt theorem and not a period bound at any floor.

Power-budget gap transfer. On a Juggler CycleMin start n ≥ 2 with word w of positive length L and oddCount o, for real 0 < C ≤ 1 and p ≥ 0, a Diophantine budget C · L^{−p} ≤ Λ = o log 3 − L log 2 gives n log n ≤ (2/C) L^{p+1} (cycleMin_length_of_gap_power). It is cycleMin_length_of_gap at ε = C L^{−p}, with gapBudget_le_one supplying ε ≤ 1; the transcendence input stays a hypothesis, as Rhin does in GapTransfer.lean. Instances: p = 13.3, C = e^{−6.1256} is Paper A Corollary 4.11; p = 4.1163051 is the Wu–Wang instance cycleMin_length_of_wuWang, length exponent 5.1163051. Floor-free. Not a halt theorem, not a kill, and not a period bound at any floor.

Floor-free period lower bound. Under the same budget C · L^{−p} ≤ Λ, a nontrivial Juggler cycle of minimum n has period L ≥ (C n log n / 2)^{1/(p+1)} (cycleMin_period_ge; Wu–Wang form cycleMin_period_ge_wuWang). This is Paper A Corollary 4.11 read as a bound on the period rather than the minimum, and it is the only proved statement in which a cycle's period grows with its minimum — the descent floor is a constant. The exponent in n rises from 1/14.3 = 0.0699 with Rhin to 1/5.1163051 = 0.1954 with Wu–Wang (wu-wang-2014-irrationality-measure-log3, |a + b log 2 + c log 3| ≥ H^{−4.1163051−ε} at a = 0, H = max(L, o) = L). Distinct from the fan-width cap of juggler_cycle_walk_fan_growth and from the REFUTED floor-level Baker transfer of juggler_cycle_gap_baker: no floor enters and nothing is excluded. At N_0 = 3.5·10^8 it forces L ≥ 74 against 780239 from the finance table, and only 58676 even at the Dirichlet floor p = 1. Not a halt theorem.

Closure threshold for the no-cycle problem. If a Diophantine budget C · L^{−p} ≤ Λ holds on every nontrivial Juggler cycle and cycle minima satisfy the matching lower bound n log n > (2/C) L^{p+1}, then every CycleMin word based at a minimum n ≥ 2 is empty: there is no nontrivial cycle (no_cycleMin_of_gap_and_minimum). Neither hypothesis is proved here; the theorem is the implication. It puts a number on the standing reopen condition of juggler_cycle_method_ceilings, "a lower bound on the cycle minimum in terms of the period": the unconditional target is n ≫ L^{5.1163051} via Wu–Wang, against n ≫ L^{14.3} via Rhin, and since p ≥ 1 for every irrational by Dirichlet no instance of the scheme ever asks for less than n ≫ L^{2}. The finance survivors sit at n log n ≍ L^{2} (ratio n log n / L^{2} in [0.164, 1.207] at L = 25781, 50508, 176251, 478245, 780239), so the gap to the unconditional target is the unbounded ratio q_{k+1}/q_k that Paper D exports. Not a halt theorem, not a proof of either hypothesis, and no cycle of any length is claimed.

For every realized finite Juggler word w, n^{3^{#O(w)}} = T_w(n)^{2^{|w|}} + Δ_w(n), where Δ is the recursively lifted accumulation of local floor remainders. Δ ≥ 0, so the power envelope is a corollary; Δ = 0 iff every local remainder vanishes; concatenation is the two-term power-gap lift, not an additive sum.

Paper A Appendix E.6, explicit formal witness. For every requested modulus q>0, c=512q-1 and b=c^3 yield two prescribed OOE first-return blocks in the same full cubic threshold band and the same section. The source, first image and endpoint are odd, all six threshold edges and first-return memberships are proved, and the final E-source parities differ. The records agree in source/first-image/endpoint/natural-aggregate residues modulo q, exact first remainder zero, and exact aggregate 2-adic valuation three. No classifier of this record can give both hidden parities correctly, even when supplied the exact common threshold and section boundary. The general positive free-b Taylor construction remains written. These blocks are not asserted periodic points; no impossibility for full absolute-value formulas or cycle-specific guards is claimed. Kernel verified.

For every natural n and finite parity itinerary w, follows n w if and only if the actual length-|w| Juggler itinerary of n equals w. The itinerary image equals the |w|-fold iterate, and images and realization compose under word concatenation.
If n and m realize the same finite Juggler word w and n ≤ m, then the image of n after w is at most the image of m after w.

If u and v are expanding itineraries (2^{|u|} < 3^{#O(u)} and 2^{|v|} < 3^{#O(v)}), then u ++ v is expanding: 2^{|u|+|v|} = 2^{|u|} 2^{|v|} < 3^{#O(u)} 3^{#O(v)}. A concatenation of expanding residual blocks is never an exponent-gap certificate. This is not a finite PE-run bound and not a halt theorem.

T(x)=m if and only if m²≤F(x)<(m+1)², with F(x)=x on the even branch and F(x)=x³ on the odd branch. The landing gap ρ=F(x)-m² satisfies 0≤ρ<2T(x)+1. Odd landing is membership of F(x) in a union of odd-m one-step preimages. These are the existing inverse-floor and remainder-window lemmas under landing names.

The normalized landing position θ=ρ/(2T+1) is a compact state for persistent odd-to-odd continuation: it occupies a proper subinterval of [0,1], or a coarse θ-bin predicts the next landing parity better than a residue class, or θ(T(x)) is a function of θ(x) and the branch. Counterexamples: on odd n≤2000, odd-odd θ occupies [0,0.997] and every tenth of [0,1]; PE-continuation landings span [0,0.995]; next-parity entropy given a θ-bin is ≈0.99, matching x mod 8; θ→θ transitions fill essentially all bins.

If y is odd and T(y) is odd, then the local remainder ρ=y³-T(y)² satisfies ρ≡y-1 (mod 8). Consequently v₂(ρ)=1 when y≡3 or 7 (mod 8), v₂(ρ)=2 when y≡5 (mod 8), and v₂(ρ)≥3 when y≡1 (mod 8) and ρ≠0. The same congruences hold for any odd square below y³; the floor T(y)=⌊y^{3/2}⌋ is not used beyond selecting an odd landing.

Persistent-expanding residual history forces a 2-adic landing restriction stronger than y mod 8: either v₂(y³-T(y)²)≥r>1 at a PE endpoint, or y≡1 (mod 16) forces v₂≥4, or the valuation locks the next residual word. Counterexamples: 365 maps to the PE endpoint 763 with v₂=1; 33≡1 (mod 16) has v₂=3; on odd n≤4000 the PE valuation table is the residue law, and v₂=1 continues as both persistent OOE and non-persistent OOEE.

OOOOOOEEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2. The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 128 together with the three-even cell z < (n+1)^8 against the coarse lower envelope n^{729} > 2^{1330}(n+1)^{512} for n ≥ 128. The computational prefix-cell first fires at N0 = 73; 128 is the algebraic cutoff. This excludes that one three-even leftover only; it is not a length-9 census, not an exclusion of the remaining eight leftovers, and not a halt theorem. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_ooooooeee.

For every k ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the even-terminating two-even leftover O^{k-2}EE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. Below 256 the argument is the existing k=6,7 leftovers, a Fin 256 table at k=8, and the fact that n ≥ 2 does not follow seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_two_even_ee. For every a ≥ 5 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. The k=0 rotation is the first-E CycleMin exclusion; the rotation at k=a+1 is the bootstrap itinerary O^b EE O^a E, excluded by last-gap ≥ 2 (OOO at N=3, or OO at N=5 with n=3 failing to follow four odds); the last even starts even; every other rotation ends odd. This upgrades the CycleMin theorem to CycleItinerary; it is not first-E transport at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-tail theorem, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

This excludes those two orientations only; the length-≤6 census is the separate row J-small-cycle-census.

No itinerary of length at most eight is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least nine. Assembly: the length-≤7 census, the formal-expansion filter on length eight, the odd-run exclusion of O^7E, Theorem 3.12 at k=8, rotation of EOOOOOOE and OEOOOOOE onto those leftovers, and the internal-E bootstrap exclusions of OOOOEOOE, OOOEOOOE, and OOEOOOOE. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_eight in LengthEightCensus.lean. Implied by Paper A Corollary 3.23 (period at least eleven). Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-ten. This is not a length-9 itinerary census and not a halt theorem.

The live count liveCount N0 N w = #{n in [1,N] : itinerary n |w| = w and n, J n, ..., J^|w| n all exceed N0} is a WeightSplit weight (liveWeight_weightSplit: the two one-letter extensions have disjoint live classes inside the parent's), and juggler_count_le_of_noMomentum instantiates the chain on it: if NoMomentum (liveWeight N0 N) x q delta d holds, then #{n in [1,N] : live for d steps, oddCount(itinerary n d) >= k} <= N a_q^d exp(c_q delta d) / x^k with a_q = 1 + (x-1) q, c_q = (x-1)/a_q. The fibrewise identity liveCount_sum_oddCount writes that count as the sum of live counts over the words with at least k odd letters. So the no-momentum hypothesis is now a proposition about itineraries of floorPower, not about an abstract weight. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

The exponent walk of any Juggler orbit satisfies u_t = o_t log2(3) - t ≡ o_t · alpha (mod 1), alpha = log2(3) - 1 = log2(3/2), because t and o_t are integers and log2(3) = 1 + alpha. Along a cycle of period L the odd count o_t takes every value 0..o, so the walk values mod 1 are exactly the rotation orbit {j·alpha}, j < o. Largest gap mod 1: 5.194e-6 at L = 478245 (o = 301739), 5.101e-6 at L = 780239 (o = 492276), 5.008e-6 at L = 1082233 (o = 682813). This is Paper A's Ostrowski layer read mod 1; it is not a period bound and not a halt theorem.

The E-tree of a seed m occupies, at generation k, the integers from m^(2^k) to (m+1)^(2^k) with internal density 2^(-k), hence natural density about 1/m at that scale, for every k. Verified exactly: m = 101, k = 1 gives 101 members at scale 1.0404e4 (density 0.009708); k = 2 gives 1040603 members at scale 1.0824e8 (density 0.009614), against 1/m = 0.009901. The burst scales of a seed are m^(2^k), one per generation.

Write c(x) = log2 log x. The scales carrying E-tree bursts of a backward-closed class are c(m) + k over its seeds m and k >= 0, so the covered scales mod 1 are {c(m) mod 1}. By J-lachesis-walk-rotation and J-lachesis-loglog-clock the cycle states of a Lachesis basin sit at c(n) + u_t, an equidistributed rotation orbit with largest gap 5.101e-6 at L = 780239, far finer than the 1.7e-4 clock defect and both far below 1. A dyadic block is a c-window of width about 1 / log y (1.46e-2 at y = 1e30, 4.34e-4 at y = 1e1000), so some cycle state's pure-E burst lands in every block out to log y = 1/5.101e-6, that is y < 1e85142; beyond that the alpha-gaps reopen. Bursts begin at n^2 (generation 1 of the minimum) and none exist below it; the full rotation is available only once c(y) - c(n) >= 1 + u_max, u_max = log2(ln M / ln n) >= 1 the cycle's walk height (Paper A: M >= (n+1)^2). Hence a Lachesis basin is not lacunary on the range n^(2^(1 + u_max)) <= y < 1e85142: it carries natural density at least about 1/n on every dyadic block there, n the cycle minimum; at n = 3.5e8 the threshold is 1e34 for u_max = 1, 1e69 for u_max = 2, 1e137 for 3. The first draft omitted the threshold. This is the third case, missing from contagion note Sec.5.3, which treats only the single seed (lacunary) and the interval [1, N0] (uniform); for the Lachesis class it upgrades Corollary 4.3 from some y in a range to every dyadic block. No fate is excluded and no period bound moves; not a halt theorem. Consolidated into the contagion note Sec. 5.3 (5 Sep 2026) as the third seed-set case, between the single point (lacunary) and the interval [1, N0] (uniform), with the exact half Lean and the every-block half labelled CONJECTURE there. Paper C is untouched; Paper A is untouched (AGENTS.md forbids editing it from a Phase-0 branch).

J-lachesis-walk-rotation does not know whether the orbit closes: the clock positions of a divergent orbit's states below y are the rotation orbit {c(n) + j alpha : j <= O(y)}, O(y) the odd count before the walk first exceeds u(y) = log2(ln y / ln n). Its basin has an E-burst in the block at y iff a point of that orbit lies within 1/ln y of c(y) mod 1; sufficient is gap(O(y)) <= 1/ln y, gap(O) the largest gap of {j alpha mod 1 : j <= O}, non-increasing in O. Thresholds O*(y) = min {O : gap(O) <= 1/ln y}: 40 at 1e12, 146 at 1e30, 252 at 1e50, 305 at 1e68, 358 at 1e100, 1635 at 1e300, 12275 at 1e1000 (O gap(O) swings between 1.26 and 6.56 with the continued fraction of alpha, three-distance). The gate is meaningful only for u(y) >= log2 3, i.e. y >= n^3: the hug band [0, log2 3) is the minimal invariant band of the walk (Lean hug_band_step_exists, narrow_band_dead, dead_zone_nonempty), and below 1 no even step is possible and at most one odd step fits (no_even_step_below_one, odd_steps_below_one_le_one), so for y < n^3 every orbit has O(y) <= 2 < O*(y) and no basin is every-block there; at n = 3.5e8 the 1e12 row (u = 0.49) is vacuous. Translated to the orbit: it must reach u(y) in at least O*(y) odd steps, so its odd share up to scale y must lie in the window (q*, s*(y)) with s* - q* = 0.0049 at 1e12, 0.0039 at 1e68, 0.0040 at 1e100, 0.0002 at 1e1000. The all-odd rate 0.585 is far outside the window at every scale. The p = 19 hug near-return rate, theta_19 / 12 = 0.00163 walk per odd step, is inside up to 1e300 but outside at 1e1000, where the gate is 0.00056; the p = 84 rate theta_84 / 53 = 5.7e-5 is inside everywhere tested (p = 1054 gives 9.5e-8). So the gate tightens with y and pushes a persistent escaper down the near-return spectrum 19, 84, 1054, ... - the cycle-period ladder of flight note Sec. 6. A Clotho basin is every-block at scale y exactly when the divergent orbit is a critical-share escaper up to that scale hugging a deep enough near-return - the kind the flight extract lets persist; a fast escaper has a lacunary basin, like a single seed. The density is then about (K / ln y) times the partial inverse sum over the states below y, K in [1, 3]; that partial sum is at least 1/n and, unlike the cycle's, is not pinned by finance. Excludes no fate; not a halt theorem.

The exact half of J-lachesis-walk-rotation; the gap sizes of the rotation orbit remain a computation. No sorry.

WalkStep u v := v = u + alphaClock or v = u - 1. hug_band_step_exists: from any u in [0, 1 + alphaClock) some step stays in the band. narrow_band_dead: if w - alphaClock <= u < 1 then no step from u stays in [0, w); dead_zone_nonempty: for 0 < w < 1 + alphaClock such a u exists in [0, w) - so the hug band [0, log2 3) is the minimal invariant band of the exponent walk. no_even_step_below_one and odd_steps_below_one_le_one (from half_lt_alphaClock, i.e. 9 > 8): below 1 no even step is possible and at most one odd step fits. Supporting bounds one_lt_logb_two_three, logb_two_three_lt_two. These are the exact reasons the Clotho every-block gate is vacuous for y < n^3 and the Lachesis bursts begin at n^2. No sorry.

Inside the hug band the parity letter is forced. band_step_forced_odd: from u < 1 a step staying in [0, 1 + alphaClock) must be the odd one, v = u + alphaClock (the even step goes negative). band_step_forced_even: from 1 <= u it must be the even one, v = u - 1 (the odd step exceeds the band). band_successor_unique: a band-confined walk has exactly one admissible successor at every point. So the walk of a band-confined orbit is the lift of the rotation by alphaClock and its parity word is the mechanical (Sturmian) word of that rotation - the hug itinerary - determined by the starting walk alone, with no freedom. No sorry.

AboveAnchor(n,w) means n follows w and every T^i(n) for i ≤ |w| is at least n. CycleMin(n,w) implies AboveAnchor(n,w). MinimalNonTerm(n) implies AboveAnchor(n,w) for every realized finite prefix w. A realized image T_w(n) < n is FiniteProgress. If the image is even and below n^2, one more even letter is FiniteProgress (the k=1 case of T(x) < n^k when x is even and x < n^{2k}). An AboveAnchor prefix plus ReturnBelow at the image is FiniteProgress. This is not cycle closure, not a no-cycle theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 and n^2 ≤ x < n^3, then an even x resets to n ≤ T(x) < n^2, and an odd x lifts to T(x) ≥ n^3. Even x < n^3 already gives T(x) < n^2 because n^3 < n^4. If that next image is also even, two even letters are FiniteProgress. On MinimalNonTerm a cube-cell even landing has odd next image. This is not a claim that a cube-cell even landing drops, not a next-letter envelope, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 and n^2 ≤ x < n^3 with x odd, then n^3 ≤ T(x) < n^5 and T(x)^2 < n^9. If T(x) is even, the first return satisfies n ≤ T^2(x) < x < n^3 and T^2(x)^4 < n^9. If T(x) is odd, then x < T^2(x) and n^4 ≤ T^2(x). An even reset that is itself even and already below n^2 is FiniteProgress; on MinimalNonTerm that case is impossible. This is not a claim that every even reset lands below n^2, not a new integer-power census, and not a halt theorem.

Knight's cancellation transports to the Juggler exactly, and its residual is precisely the state dependence of the slack -- so the method dies at the Terras/FD wall and nowhere else. KNIGHT'S THREE PARTS. (i) Two members of one cycle, since Cohn makes the reverse of an aperiodic upper Christoffel word a rotation of it. (ii) An ADDITIVE cocycle: the Bohm-Sontacchi charge g is a function of the WORD alone, so the split v_h = 1u0, v_h^R = 0u1 gives g(v_h) = 2g(u) + 3^(x-1) and g(v_h^R) = 6g(u) + 2^(k-1), and 3f(v_h) - f(v_h^R) + 1 cancels the shared g(u). (iii) The leftover 2^(k-1)/(2^k - 3^x) is not an integer because the gap is odd. THE TRANSPORT. Part (i) is free, Cohn being a fact about words, so v_h and v_h^R are one Juggler cycle read at two points. Part (ii) transports formally through the kernel-checked multiplicative cocycle J-normalized-relative-slack, 1 + q_(uv) = (1+q_u)^(3^(#O(v))) (1+q_v)^(2^|u|): expanding w = O u E from n and w' = E u O from n' gives 1+q_w = (1+q_O @ n)^(3^p) (1+q_u @ J(n))^2 (1+q_E @ t)^(2^(m+1)) and 1+q_w' = (1+q_E @ n')^(3^(p+1)) (1+q_u @ J(n'))^6 (1+q_O @ t')^(2^(m+1)), so the multiplicative analogue of 3f - f^R is cube-and-divide, which cancels the shared middle exponent exactly, 3*2 - 6 = 0. THE RESIDUAL IS THE WHOLE STORY: (1+q_w)^3/(1+q_w') = [endpoint terms] * ((1+q_u @ J(n))/(1+q_u @ J(n')))^6. For Collatz the corresponding residual is identically 1, g(u) being literally the same integer in both expressions; for the Juggler 1 + q is a function of the word AND the state, the middle word being read at J(n) along one rotation and J(n') along the other, so the residual is a sixth power of their ratio. VERIFIED with exact rationals: the residual identity holds on all 15 word-pairs at length 6 taken at least starts, and on all 1354 instances obtained by pairing every realizing start below 6000 with the mirror's least start; the two middle slacks coincide in NONE of them. So Knight's method transports and fails at exactly the dichotomy J-juggler-is-collatz-one-exponential-up names: Collatz's word data is arithmetic and free (Terras), the Juggler's is state-dependent and open (Hypothesis FD). The same wall, met in a new place, which is the value of the row -- it says the obstruction is not incidental to this method. WHAT IT LEAVES, SCOPED. On a return 1 + q = n^(3^o - 2^L), so the left side is (n^3/n')^G with G the gap: a perfect G-th power, and Knight's parity step becomes a Catalan-flavoured condition. Hence a Juggler cycle carrying the Christoffel word AND having equal middle slacks at its two reverse-conjugate readings would force an explicit product of endpoint slacks to be a perfect G-th power. That equality is a strong Diophantine coincidence, is not conjectured here either way, and without it there is no exclusion. NO JUGGLER CYCLE IS EXCLUDED, no floor is raised, N_0 is unchanged and Paper A is untouched. This does not reopen J-cycle-near-tight-monochrome or J-affine-n-gap-escapes-dominance, both REFUTED in this neighbourhood; it is a different combination and it claims less.

A(phi) is not an independent unknown: the update determines the tail amplitude from the boundary fraction through an explicit multiplicative cocycle over the rotation. THE DERIVATION, which is algebra and is exact. J-phase-shift-is-one-update-and-R-halves makes a phase shift by the slope exactly one application of the update, Pi_(phi+s) = T_b Pi_phi / (1 - b Pi_phi(0)/2). Pushing the tail form A (m + c) r*^m through it closes in the same form: a non-rising step gives c' = c - s and A' = A / (2(1-s)); a rising step gives c' = c + (1-s) and A' = A / (2 s (1 - R/2)) with R = Pi_phi(0). THE NON-RISING MULTIPLIER DEPENDS ON NOTHING BUT THE SLOPE. At 306/485 the prediction is 1.3547486 and the five occurrences in fourteen steps read 1.3549281, 1.3549291, 1.3549301, 1.3549280, 1.3549293 -- agreeing with each other to 1e-6 and with the prediction to 1.3e-4, the gap being the cap and the fit window, not scatter. The rising branch tracks its R-dependent prediction to 7.9e-5 while that prediction itself varies over 0.8228, 0.8467, 0.8274, 0.8521. THE c RECURSION IS THE SAWTOOTH AND THE BRANCH IS THE RISE LETTER. c' = c - s or c + (1-s) is exactly c = gamma - phi mod 1, and the wrap occurs precisely when frac(phi) >= 1 - s, which is precisely b(phi) = 1. That settles the lattice-branch false trail recorded in J-profile-is-linear-times-geometric-in-the-line-coordinate: the branch was never something to guess, it is the Sturmian letter. AND IT REPRODUCES THE ERGODIC IDENTITY BY A SECOND ROUTE. For A to be single-valued on the circle the cocycle must average to zero, which reads integral over {b=1} of log(1 - R/2) = -(1-s) log(2(1-s)) - s log(2s) = H(s) - log 2 with H the binary entropy. At s = BETA that right-hand side IS log rho identically, to 8.3e-17, because the Chernoff rate is beta^(-beta) (1-beta)^(beta-1) / 2. So the cocycle recovers J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate's log rho = integral log(1 - b R / 2), which that row derives from the count recursion instead. WHAT THE PROFILE NOW COSTS: one constant gamma for the shape, and the boundary fraction R for everything else. The three unknowns the family started with -- shape, zero, amplitude -- are down to R, which is already the laboratory's clean coordinate. WHAT IS NOT PROVED: that the tail form holds at all. That is measured (residual 2.4e-4 at cap 1200, falling like cap^-2) and the Lean module says so explicitly; these seven theorems are the consequences of the form, kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. Machinery: amplitude_cocycle_check. The update is proved in both branches, update_true_tail for a rising step and update_false_tail for a non-rising one, and the multipliers they produce are rising_multiplier_base for the rising case and nonrising_multiplier for the other. The two algebraic identities the cocycle rests on are one_div_one_add_tailRoot and tailRoot_div_one_add, the two shifts at r = (1-s)/s.

R(phi) is piecewise constant, changing exactly at the rotation orbit -- the same orbit psi jumps on -- and that explains why the single-jump model of f fails. THE ARGUMENT. The backward word has w_j(phi) = 1{frac(phi - (j+1)BETA) >= 1 - BETA}, and the set of phi satisfying that is an arc of length BETA with endpoints j BETA and (j+1) BETA. So a length-K word flips only at {k BETA : k = 0..K}, and is constant on every interval free of those points; Pi_phi, computed from the word alone, is therefore constant there too. R is a step function whose jump set is the orbit. VERIFIED. On a uniform grid of 8192 phases against a 1200-step word, R changes at 1100 grid steps, none of them strictly inside a gap, and no gap boundary without a change. Jump sizes decay: 0.1171 at k = 0, then 0.0358, 0.0179, 0.0089, 0.0068. WHY IT MATTERS. f = log(1 - b R / 2) - log rho inherits R's jumps on top of its own at 1 - BETA, so f is NOT a single-jump function. That is why measured |f_hat(q)| falls far below the pure-jump prediction |J|/(2 pi q), by a factor 37 at q = 84, and why the reading |psi_hat(q_j)| ~ |J| a_(j+1)/(4 pi^2) -- proportionality to the next partial quotient -- is NOT confirmed, its ratios running 0.03 to 4.7 across the convergents. That prediction is recorded as refuted in the form stated; a version accounting for R's own jumps is untested. NEW MACHINERY, WITH ITS LIMIT STATED. boundary_fraction_at_phases computes R at ARBITRARY phases rather than along the orbit, which removes the turn-count ceiling of J-psi-bounded-only-at-resolvable-resonances. But its convergence is slower than the d^(-2) of J-killed-walk-forgets-polynomially: against the exact forward profile the relative error runs 0.119, 0.037, 0.019, 0.008 at steps = 300, 900, 1500, 2500, about steps^(-1.5), so a few thousand steps buys about a percent. That is ample for locating structure and NOT ample for amplitudes, since the Fourier coefficients at deep resonances are smaller than the error. The deep resonance question therefore remains open, and the grid does not settle it. IN LEAN. The argument above is now machine-checked. `backWord_iff_fract_lt` is the whole of it: the letter, written against the anchor (j+1)*b, holds exactly when fract (phi - j*b) < b, so it is the indicator of an arc anchored at j*b. From that, `backWord_of_mem_arc` gives the letter on over [j*b, (j+1)*b) and `not_backWord_of_mem_gap` gives it off over [(j+1)*b, j*b + 1), which are the two arcs the orbit cuts; `backWord_congr` says the letter sees the phase only through its position relative to the anchor. All print [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. What is NOT formalised is the step from the word to R -- that needs the profile, hence the convergence that J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate still lacks -- so the Lean covers the exact half of this row and not the measured half.

A convergent's rise word errs in |s - s'| T^2 of its first T letters, a full power of T above the naive bound. THE NAIVE BOUND IS FALSE. One expects ceil(t*s) - ceil(t*s') to be monotone, so the two words differ at most as often as it moves, giving 2(T|s-s'| + 1) disagreements in [0,T]. That predicts about 2 errors for 665/1054 against beta out to T = 32000; the measured count is 12. The difference OSCILLATES rather than climbing -- it equals t(s-s') + delta(ts) - delta(ts') with each delta in [0,1), so it crosses back and forth -- and total variation does not bound the count. THE CORRECT LAW comes from the arc form already formalised as backWord_iff_fract_lt: the letter at t is a rise iff frac(t*s) lies in (1-s, 1), the two orbits separate linearly as |frac(t*s) - frac(t*s')| = t|s-s'|, and equidistribution integrates the straddling probability to sum over t<T of 2t|s-s'| = |s-s'| T^2. It saturates at T/2, where the words are independent. MEASURED against beta at 306/485, observed over predicted: 1.09, 1.05, 1.03, 1.02, 1.01 at T = 8000, 16000, 32000, 64000, 128000 -- a 16-fold range converging to one from above. Deeper convergents are pre-asymptotic because the orbit has not yet come near the endpoint: 665/1054 reads 0.00, 0.00, 0.31, 0.65, 0.81 over the same window, climbing to one. THE PREFIX LENGTH IS STILL q_(k+1), as classical Sturmian theory says -- the first error sits at 484, 568, 25780, 24726 for 306/485, 53/84, 665/1054, 15601/24727, alternating between q - 1 and about q_(k+1) + q with the side from which the convergent approaches. What the T^2 law governs is how fast errors ACCUMULATE after the prefix ends, not where it ends. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: it is the letter-level reason J-sturmian-driving-is-uniform-in-q holds. 665/1054 and 15601/24727 reproduce beta's word exactly out to t = 24726, so their forward runs are identical there and only their limit profiles -- fixed points of different periodic operators -- can differ, which is why their Yaglom constants agree to six digits at d = 4000 and only five at d = 32000. Machinery: sturmian_word_disagreements. No bound moves.

PROVED, and elementary. Write N_d for the number of words of length d with o_t >= ceil(t BETA) at every t <= d, and P_d = N_d/2^d. If the barrier does not rise at step d, that is ceil((d+1)BETA) = ceil(d BETA), then N_(d+1) = 2 N_d and so P_(d+1) = P_d EXACTLY. Proof: let w be a surviving word of length d and x any letter. The odd count is monotone, so o_(d+1) = o_d + x >= o_d >= ceil(d BETA) = ceil((d+1)BETA), and w ++ [x] survives; conversely a survivor of length d+1 restricts to one of length d. So (w, x) -> w ++ [x] is a bijection from survivors of length d times two letters onto survivors of length d+1. THIS SETTLES J-sturmian-zero-step-leaves-the-raw-jump-invariant. When s_k = 0 both depths bracketing k BETA have a non-rising barrier, so P at each is individually unchanged under d -> d+1, hence so is any combination -- and the 1/rho of J-psi-amplitude-ratio-is-one-over-rho-at-the-sturmian-zeros is what the rho^d d^(-3/2) normalisation makes of one free step. CORRECTION. That row states that the two terms are NOT individually preserved and that a proof needs a bijection on their difference. Both are false, checked: at s_k = 0 each term is preserved on its own, to floating-point zero, and no bijection on a difference is needed or exists. The claim was asserted without testing it and is withdrawn. LEAN. The content is survives_succ_of_no_rise, with survives_of_survives_succ the converse restriction and noRise_iff_le_ceil characterising the non-rising step as ((t+1) b <= ceil(t b)), which for b = BETA is the Sturmian condition indexing s_k; barrier and barrierRise name the two quantities. Kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. The cardinality bookkeeping N_(d+1) = 2 N_d is the bijection above and is not formalised; it is one line and is stated here rather than in Lean. SCOPE. This proves an identity about the counting function, not anything about psi's existence, which remains a local limit theorem for a killed walk against a Sturmian barrier and is untouched. It also explains the residual drift recorded in the earlier rows: the measured ratios approach 1/rho from above and slide because of the d^(-3/2) factor, not because the identity is approximate. It is not approximate.

PROVED, and it closes the amplitude question in both cases at once. Let N_d count the words of length d with o_t >= ceil(t BETA) at every t <= d, let M_d count those of them with o_d = ceil(d BETA) exactly -- sitting ON the barrier -- and let b_d = ceil((d+1)BETA) - ceil(d BETA). Then N_(d+1) = 2 N_d - b_d M_d, an exact integer identity, checked for d = 1..58 with no floating point in the recursion and agreeing with non_contracting at d = 10, 25, 40. Equivalently P_(d+1) = P_d - b_d Q_d / 2 with P_d = N_d/2^d and Q_d = M_d/2^d the mass on the barrier. PROOF. Every survivor of length d has two extensions. If b_d = 0 both survive, by PaperBBarrierStep.survives_succ_of_no_rise. If b_d = 1, a survivor strictly above the barrier still keeps both (survives_succ_of_above_barrier, since one more odd letter cannot be needed when the count already exceeds the old ceiling by at least one), and a survivor exactly on the barrier loses precisely the even extension and only that one (dies_iff_on_barrier). So exactly b_d M_d extensions are lost. All three are kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone; the cardinality bookkeeping is the sentence above and is not formalised. WHAT IT SETTLES. J-non-rising-barrier-step-doubles-the-count is the b_d = 0 case. The b_d = 1 case had NO rule -- J-psi-amplitude-rule-is-second-order-in-the-sturmian-word could only report that the ratio splits by position in the Sturmian run, 0.983 against 0.932. That split is now identified: since the two depths bracketing k BETA share b = s_k, the amplitude recursion is a_(k+1) - a_k = -s_k (Q_(d-) - Q_(d+)) / 2, a difference of BOUNDARY OCCUPATIONS. It was never a numerical pattern. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT COORDINATE. Q_d is boundary local time for the killed walk, which is what a local limit theorem produces; the measured envelope a_k ~ 1.12 k^(-1.09) becomes a statement about how Q_d varies between bracketing depths. So psi's existence, still open, acquires a shape it did not have: instead of 'some limit exists' the target is the asymptotics of Q_d for a walk killed at a Sturmian barrier. Nothing here proves that, and no bound moves. THE CARDINALITY BOOKKEEPING IS NOW FORMALISED (18 September 2026). This row records the sentence joining the three branches as not formalised. PaperBCertificateRecursion.neverNegCount_add_minimalCertCount proves it as a Finset cardinality identity in Nat arithmetic, and minimalCertCount_succ identifies its minimalCertCount (d+1) with this row's b_d M_d via minimalCertWords_succ. Every declaration involved rests on subsets of Mathlib's three axioms.

R's jump amplitudes halve exactly at every Sturmian zero, and the reason is one line. THE RULE. Crossing k BETA flips exactly two letters of the backward word, w_(k-1) from 1 to 0 and w_k from 0 to 1, so R's jump there is a difference of two word-driven runs and is directly computable. Measured at k = 0..21 the ratio a_(k+1)/a_k is 0.50000 to five decimals at k = 2, 5, 8, 10, 13, 16, 18 -- exactly the k with s_k = 0 -- and unsettled elsewhere, running 0.988, 0.773, 1.166, 0.895, 1.258, 1.415, 1.060, 1.388. THE MECHANISM. A non-rising step is m -> m + X, so m = 0 is reachable only from m = 0 and the update sends pi(0) to pi(0)/2; it also preserves total mass, so no renormalisation intervenes. A boundary PERTURBATION therefore halves, and R's jump with it. A rising step mixes in pi(1), which is why no rule of this kind holds at s_k = 1. Formalised as PaperBBarrierStep.update, update_false_at_zero, update_false_sub_at_zero and update_true_at_zero, kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. This is the exact companion of J-non-rising-barrier-step-doubles-the-count: a non-rising step doubles the count and halves the boundary value, both for the same reason, that nothing can fall below a barrier that did not move. WHY THE RATIOS ARE TRUSTWORTHY WHERE THE AMPLITUDES ARE NOT. Doubling the word length from 1500 to 3000 moves every amplitude by 1.2 to 1.3 percent. That is a COMMON scale factor, since both sides of each jump are run identically and for the same length, so it cancels in the ratio and not in the value: the absolute amplitudes carry the convergence error of J-boundary-fraction-is-a-step-function-on-the-orbit, the ratios do not. That is the reverse of the usual situation in this thread, where ratios were the suspect quantity.

Advancing the phase by BETA is exactly one application of the update map, and the consequence is that R halves outright at every non-rising phase. THE RELATION. w_j(phi + BETA) = 1{frac(phi - j BETA) >= 1 - BETA} = w_(j-1)(phi), so shifting the phase shifts the backward word one place and prepends a letter -- that is, applies one more update at the end: Pi_(phi+BETA) = T_(b(phi)) Pi_phi / (1 - b(phi) Pi_phi(0) / 2). Verified at random phases with residual 0.0e+00, the mass lost being exactly Pi_phi(0)/2 when b = 1 and exactly zero when b = 0. THE COROLLARY. At b(phi) = 0 the update preserves mass, so the normaliser is 1, and PaperBBarrierStep.update_false_at_zero gives T_0 Pi(0) = Pi(0)/2. Hence R(phi + BETA) = R(phi)/2 whenever phi < 1 - BETA. Confirmed to 1.6e-16 at phases away from the switch point and to 1e-12 against the independent forward orbit profile; at b = 1 it fails as it must, the observed ratios being 2.63 and 3.26 rather than 1. THIS SUBSUMES J-r-jumps-halve-at-the-sturmian-zeros: if R itself halves under the shift then so does any difference of two of its values, which is what that row measured. It also explains why the jump recursion delta_(k+1) = T_(s_k) delta_k is exact at s_k = 0, with residuals at machine epsilon, and fails at s_k = 1 with relative errors 0.10 to 0.50 -- at a rising step the two sides of a jump lose DIFFERENT amounts of mass, so the normalisers differ and the map is no longer linear on differences. WHAT IT IS. A transfer-operator cocycle over the rotation: the quasi-stationary family is generated by iterating one of two explicit maps according to the Sturmian word, and every structural fact recorded about R and psi in this thread is a consequence of that single relation. What remains unproved is unchanged -- that the iteration converges, which is the quasi-stationary statement of J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate. IN LEAN. THE RELATION is `backWord_shift` of PaperBBackwardWord, which proves w_(j+1)(phi + b) = w_j(phi) and is kernel-clean; paired with `PaperBBarrierStep.update_false_at_zero` for the halving, both halves of this row's mechanism are now machine-checked. The natural coupling proof for the quasi-stationary limit does not close: restricting to the light-tail class gives an invariant cone but no contraction. THE CONE IS INVARIANT, EXACTLY, and for a reason with no content beyond addition -- the updated value at a site is an average of two neighbouring old values, so the bound at the two sites adds. `update_true_ratio` and `update_false_ratio` prove pi(m+1) <= s pi(m) is carried forward by both updates in the bulk, at every s, kernel-clean. IT FAILS AT THE BARRIER AND ONLY THERE. A non-rising step sends mass up, so the updated ratio at m = 0 is at least 1 and no cone with s < 1 survives it (`boundary_ratio_at_least_one`). The defect is one site wide: measured, the bulk ratios sit at the initial value to four decimals while the ratio at m = 0 oscillates over 0.45, 1.45, 0.86, 1.67. BIRKHOFF STILL FAILS. On the light-tail class the Hilbert projective metric does decay to zero -- 6.22 to 0.011 and 23.92 to 0.0055 over d = 0 to 12000 -- but POLYNOMIALLY, not geometrically. Fitting log d_H against d and against log d over d = 2000..12000 gives residual standard deviations 0.20 and 0.011, a factor of twenty in favour of the polynomial, with exponents -1.865, -1.962, -1.606. An earlier reading of the same data over d <= 2000 showed the local exponent RISING, 0.74 to 1.90, which looks like eventual geometry and is transient; the longer window settles at d^-2. So the cone restriction does not restore the contraction that J-no-exponential-weight-restores-the-gap denies, and this is that same criticality seen from the projective side. WHAT SURVIVES. d_H is summable at d^-2, and a summable non-contractive argument is a different proof from Birkhoff -- it needs the polynomial rate as an input rather than producing it, which is the original problem. The invariant cone stands as the structure such an argument would use. No bound moves and no fate is excluded.

PROVED IN LEAN, for every pair d <= K, over the naturals: 2^(K-d) * N_d = sum_{j=d+1}^{K} 2^(K-j) * M_j + N_K, where N_d = neverNegCount d counts the length-d words with no contracting prefix and M_j = minimalCertCount j counts those contracting for the first time at j. Divided by 2^K it reads N_d/2^d = sum_{j=d+1}^{K} M_j/2^j + N_K/2^K, so the survivor density at depth d is the mass of the certificates still to come plus whatever has not decided by K; letting K run off leaves the survivor density as the tail mass of the minimal certificates. The proof is neverNegCount_add_minimalCertCount summed under Nat.le_induction and nothing else, so no rational, no limit and no real number enters the statement or the proof. WHY IT WAS WORTH PROVING rather than leaving measured. The telescoped form was established on 2026-09-19 in rational arithmetic at d = 4, 12, 24, 40, 60 against a cap of 200 (J-winkler-sandwich-holds-on-the-laboratory-counts, and the test in test_collatz_bridge.py). THE EMPTY-WINDOW UNIFICATION, RESOLVED: it is two theorems sharing one definition, not one theorem controlling five things, and the count of five was inflated. Pass of 2026-09-19, nine agents, with an independent proposer and adversary reaching the same split from opposite instructions. GROUP A, consequences of a length BEING free. At a free length the survivor set is a full cylinder, neverNegWords (d+1) = neverNegWords d x {E,O} (neverNegWords_succ_of_window_empty), so every additive functional of it factorises over the two extensions (sum_neverNegWords_succ_of_window_empty, any AddCommMonoid, any f). The recorded instances are that one theorem read through three summands: f = 1 gives the density plateaus; a character gives the good-set Wiener-norm plateau; f w = a^oddCount w gives the tilted count, which multiplies by exactly 1 + a. GROUP B, WHICH lengths are free. That is minimalCert_exists_iff, and the pass named its content: the carrying lengths are Nat.log 2 (3^o) + 1, i.e. A020914 and Winkler's m_r + 1 (certWindow_iff_natLog, minimalCert_exists_iff_natLog). Winkler's equality orders live here and not in Group A, and they are not the same structure either -- his records are about ORDERS r, the empty-window theorem about LENGTHS d. WHAT THE COUNT OF FIVE WAS DOUBLE-COUNTING. Certificate lengths, the sandwich's support and the A054414/A020914 Beatty split are one statement written three ways. The 1/rho jump law is the density plateau again: its weight (2 theta)^(n-1) depends on the length and not on the word, so as a functional it is f = 1 up to a constant, and its row was already tagged REPARAMETERIZATION and already retracted as a finding. The tilted count is the genuine weight summand and was not on the list at all. TWO CLAIMS WITHDRAWN. And the claim that the empty-window theorem controls the lengths a positive Collatz cycle can have rests on reading prefix_bound_of_min as excluding contracting prefixes; the Lean proves a cap on x+1, not that exclusion. SUFFICIENT, NOT NECESSARY. A plateau is evidence of a free length, not proof of one: d = 5 is not free, N_5 = 4 against 2 N_4 = 6, yet the good-set Wiener norm is unchanged there. Paper B section 7's per-letter coefficient rule, as an identity rather than a table. For a word w over {O,E} write p_q = 3/2 if letter q is O and 1/2 if it is E, and e_t = prod_{q<=t} p_q, so J^t(n) sits at scale n^{e_t}. For letters s < t the coefficient of the phase variable theta_s inside letter t's phase is (k/2) E at exponent e_{t-1} - e_s, where E = prod_{q=s+1}^{t-1} p_q. Proof: letter t's wave is e(k J^{t-1}/2), and J^{t-1} depends on theta_s only through the chain of power maps between them; composing power maps composes to a single power, so the chain contributes exactly the product of its step exponents. The identity that makes this a rule and not a table is E = e_{t-1}/e_s, checked on every word of length 3..10 and every pair s < t -- 75768 instances, no exception. It reproduces the three monomials Paper B prints: (3k/4) n^{9/8} at (w, t, s) = (OOOO, 4, 2), C = (9k/16) n^{3/16} at (OOOEO, 5, 1), and B = (3k/4) v^{1/4} at (EOO, 3, 1). LEAN, 14 September 2026: `chain_rule` in PaperBChainRule.lean proves E = e_{t-1}/e_s for every prefix and every intervening block, over exact rationals, on the back of `iter_split` (the product over a concatenation splits) and `iter_pos`; `iter_nil` is its unit case. The three printed monomials are `printed_thm53`, `printed_thm63_C` and `printed_thm63_B`, each the rule evaluated at its own word. The E < 2 linearisation criterion of Paper B section 7, as an identity. With the notation of J-paper-b-defect-coefficient-chain, the squared-defect term in letter t's phase sits at exponent e_{t-1} - 2 e_s, and since e_{t-1} = e_s E this equals e_s (E - 2). As e_s > 0 always, the second-order exponent is negative exactly when E < 2: linearising theta_s inside letter t is safe precisely on that condition. The criterion is therefore not a threshold fitted to the words that happen to survive -- it is the point at which the second-order term stops growing, and 2 is forced by the squaring and nothing else. Checked as an identity on every word of length 3..10 and every pair s < t (75768 instances, no exception), with the sign of the second-order exponent agreeing with E < 2 in every instance. Positive second-order exponents at defects a kernel keeps exact are harmless because they are never expanded, which is why only the deepest blocked defect is tested. LEAN, 14 September 2026: `second_order` in PaperBChainRule.lean is the identity e_{t-1} - 2 e_s = e_s (E - 2), and `linearise_iff` is the equivalence the second-order exponent is negative iff E < 2, for every prefix and block; `no_linearise_iff` is the same statement from the other side, and `two_odd_not_safe` and `odd_even_safe` are the two smallest instances (E = 9/4 fails, E = 3/4 passes). The proof uses nothing about 3/2 and 1/2 beyond positivity, which is the content of the claim that 2 is forced by the squaring. Kernel-checked. Not a proof that any word contracts.

Paper B section 7's composed map is the exponent walk of the Paper C collision work, and its linearisation criterion is a unit climb of that walk. With the notation of J-paper-b-defect-coefficient-chain, e_t = 3^(o_t) / 2^t exactly, where o_t is the number of odd letters up to t (`iter_eq_pow`). Taking log base 2 gives e_t = 2^(u_t) with u_t = o_t log2(3) - t, which is the walk J-live-set-ladder-factorisation splits at, J-damping-at-running-minimum is about, and J-dominant-defect-at-walk-minimum measures the climb of. Hence E = e_{t-1}/e_s = 2^(u_{t-1} - u_s), and E < 2 says exactly that the walk climbs by less than one unit between the defect at letter s and the wave at letter t. Two consequences. (i) The criterion is an exact integer inequality in the counts: with a odd and b even letters in the block, E < 2 iff 3^a < 2^(a+b+1) (`lt_two_iff_counts`), so it never needs a logarithm or a float. (ii) It does not see the order of the block, only the two counts (`iter_eq_of_counts`, `lt_two_congr`), which is immediate from the closed form and invisible in the product form; 45 count pairs cover every block arising in words of length up to 10. The supporting declarations are `oddCount`, `oddCount_cons_O` and `oddCount_cons_E`. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. This is a reformulation and not an improvement: no bound moves, no density exponent changes, and the collision hypothesis is untouched. What it buys is that two screens developed separately are one test in one coordinate, and that E is literally the amplification factor A_k of J-dominant-defect-at-walk-minimum rather than an analogue of it.

All three conditions of Paper B section 7's screen are functions of the exponent walk u_t = o_t log2(3) - t alone, and two of them are unit conditions on it. With e_t = 2^(u_t) (J-paper-b-E-is-the-exponent-walk): the branch-run condition e_{s-1} < 2 is u_{s-1} < 1, an absolute height; the linearisation criterion E < 2 is u_{t-1} - u_s < 1, a climb; and the 9/4 stopping threshold e_{t-1} - e_s > 9/4 is 2^(u_{t-1}) - 2^(u_s) > 9/4. Checked over every word of length 3 to 11: 4204 letters with a blocked defect, no mismatch on any of the three. Non-contraction is a condition on the same walk (1 <= e_t, i.e. u_t >= 0), so the property defining a contractor and the property tripping the branch-run hypothesis are one constraint at thresholds 0 and 1. At step two the first forces the second: a prefix not contracted by its second letter must be OO, since E gives u_1 = -1 and OE gives u_2 = log2(3) - 2 < 0, so e_2 = 9/4 > 2, the branch-run threshold, because 3 > 2^(3/2) (`noncontracting_two_forces`, kernel-checked; `two_lt_nine_quarters` is the threshold comparison). Every one of the 140 contractors at depths 4 to 13 begins OO. The forcing does NOT extend along the word and is not claimed to: the walk is not monotone, and OOOEOOEE has a blocked defect at s = 5 with u_4 = 0.755, below the threshold. What is measured rather than proved is that from depth ten the hypothesis fires on every contractor anyway (12 of 12, 30 of 30, 85 of 85), and that the least peak a contractor's walk can have rises 1.170, 1.340, 1.510 with depth. Not a halt theorem, no bound moves, and no density exponent changes.

Paper B's non-contracting word count and Paper C's bad-word count are one function at two levels. Both are the same dynamic program over (steps, odd letters), written independently in paper_b_prefix_count and collision_large_sieve, and N_d = bad_word_count(0, d) exactly for d = 1 to 16 (1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 19, 38, 64, 128, 226, 367, 734, 1295, 2114). The O-rooting costs nothing either, since a word starting E has u_1 = -1. TRANSFER, and its limit. Because the counts coincide, Paper C's tools apply to Paper B's object; the sharpest, the Wiener-Hopf ladder factorisation at the walk minimum (J-live-set-ladder-factorisation), does specialise correctly and computes with exact identity error 0 at L = 0.05 and 0.25. But it degenerates there: at L -> 0 the argmin sits at the start with probability 1, so every word is a positive excursion and the split has no descending side. Every declaration reachable from here is an identity, a constant, or a threshold; not one of them is an estimate.' That was accurate and is the reason 49 axiom-checked declarations do not amount to corroboration, against Paper A's 335 and Paper C's 409. WHAT IS NOW PROVED. PaperBChernoff, six theorems, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. one_sub_inv_lt_log gives the strict form 1 - x^(-1) < log x for x > 0, x not 1, from Real.add_one_lt_exp. klDiv_pos is strict Gibbs: 0 < D(p||q) whenever p is not q, which the fate layer's klDiv_nonneg does not give. theta_eq_exp_neg_klDiv bridges the manuscript's printed theta q = q^(-q)(1-q)^(q-1)/2 to exp(-D(q||1/2)) -- the same identity the 16 September re-audit checks numerically to 1e-12. theta_lt_one is then the estimate: theta q < 1 for every q in (0,1) other than 1/2, with theta_pos and theta_pow_lt in the form Theorem 6.1 uses. WHY IT IS THE RIGHT ONE. klDiv_nonneg gives only theta <= 1, and a bound of 1^(d-1)/2 is vacuous at every depth; the strictness is what makes Theorem 6.1's density bound DECAY rather than merely fail to grow. It is the single inequality the whole of Section 6 is aimed at. WIRED IN, not merely present: the module is imported by the Paper B barrel, the barrel's claim is corrected to say one declaration is now an estimate and the rest are not, and the manuscript cites theta_lt_one at the point where theta_d < 1 is used. WHAT IS STILL NOT FORMALISED, and the module says so in its own header: the exponential Markov step, the binomial generating function, and the passage from surviving words to natural density are all still written mathematics. This formalises the inequality those steps are aimed at, not the steps. So Paper B's analytic core remains unformalised and the barrel still says the trust-boundary discussion governs. No bound moves.

The FD step is formalised as an inference, and Theorem 6.1 stays conditional -- which is what the manuscript already says and what the formalisation must not quietly improve on. WHAT FD IS. A HYPOTHESIS, not a result: 'Hypothesis FD. For every fixed d >= 1 and every odd-rooted word w of length d, #{n <= N : word_d(n) = w} = 2^(-d) N + o_w(N). No common error rate in d is assumed.' Theorem 6.1 is headed 'conditional density-one certificate theorem' and the manuscript's own table lists the density-one certificates as conditional on FD. So the task was never to prove the step; it was to state the hypothesis and derive the conclusion. WHAT IS PROVED. PaperBDensity, three theorems, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. density_of_finite_union: if each of finitely many classes has density r, their union has density card * r. That is the entire content of 'FD and a finite sum over surviving words show that the natural density is their number divided by 2^d' -- FD gives r = 2^(-d) for one class and finite additivity does the rest, which is exactly why the hypothesis is needed at each fixed d separately and why no uniformity in d is asserted. tendsto_zero_of_eventually_le: a nonnegative quantity eventually below c d for every d, with c d -> 0, tends to zero -- the 'letting d -> infinity proves the assertion' at the end of the proof. exceptional_density_zero combines them in the shape Theorem 6.1 uses. THE CHAIN NOW READS, formally: the bad words number at most 2^n theta q ^ n (PaperBMarkov.chernoff_density), theta q < 1 (PaperBChernoff.theta_lt_one), at the optimal tilt the two agree exactly (PaperBMarkov.tilt_gives_theta), and a density dominated at every depth by a vanishing bound is zero (PaperBDensity). WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED, and the module header says so: Hypothesis FD itself, which is open; and that the bad set at depth d IS a finite union of word classes, which is the combinatorial reading of word_d and stays written mathematics. Theorem 6.1 is not formalised. Its inference from FD is. Paper B's barrel now names four modules beyond identities and thresholds and still says the analytic core -- Theorem 4.11, Theorem 5.4, Appendices A to C -- is unformalised. No bound moves.

Paper B Theorems 5.2-5.4, assembly half. Let certifiedWords d be the length-d parity words with a contracting prefix. (i) Their counts are 13, 28, 56, 115 at d = 4, 5, 6, 7, so the certificate densities are 13/16, 7/8, 7/8, 115/128; depth six adds nothing. (ii) At depth five the cylinders of E, OE, OOEE, OOOEE, OOEOE have sizes 16, 8, 2, 1, 1, are pairwise disjoint, and their union is exactly certifiedWords 5 (five_cylinders_cover, five_cylinders_card_sum) — so the printed 1/2+1/4+1/16+1/32+1/32 = 7/8 is the cylinder arithmetic and not a free-standing rational identity (printed_measures_are_counts). (iii) For every N the starts in {1,...,N} certified by depth five number classCount E N + classCount OE N + classCount OOEE N + classCount OOOEE N + classCount OOEOE N (certifiedCount_five_eq), via sum_classCount_cylinder and itinerary_take. (iv) 5/6 < 23/24 < 47/48 < 127/128 < 1 with N^e <= N^f for e <= f and N >= 1, which is the absorption the proofs assume.
